title: AC Sources & Circuits

notes.heading: 1. Sinusoidal RMS, Half-Cycle Average, Form Factor & Crest Factor
notes.proseLatex: For a pure sine wave $v(t) = V_m\sin(\omega t + \phi)$ ($\omega = 2\pi f$), effective heating value is $V_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_m}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707\,V_m$ and half-cycle rectified average is $V_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2V_m}{\pi} \approx 0.637\,V_m$ (full-cycle average is $0$). Form factor is $K_f = \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{V_{\text{avg}}} = \frac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}} \approx 1.11$ and peak/crest factor is $K_p = \frac{V_m}{V_{\text{rms}}} = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$ (for a symmetric square wave, $K_f = K_p = 1$; for a half-wave rectified sine, $V_{\text{rms}} = V_m/2$ and $V_{\text{avg}} = V_m/\pi$!).

keyFormulas.label: Sine, Half-Wave & Square-Wave RMS / Form Factor
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Recall exact RMS, average, form factor, and peak factor of standard waveforms.

notes.heading: 2. Series RLC Impedance, Resonance, Q-Factor & Bandwidth
notes.proseLatex: Series RLC impedance is $Z = R + j(X_L - X_C)$ where $X_L = \omega L$ (current LAGS voltage by $90^\circ$ in pure $L$) and $X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C}$ (current LEADS voltage by $90^\circ$ in pure $C$), with $|Z| = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$. At series resonance ($X_L = X_C \implies f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$), impedance hits its MINIMUM $|Z|_{\min} = R$, current hits its MAXIMUM $V/R$ at UNITY power factor ($\cos\phi = 1$), and reactive voltages magnify to $Q V$ where quality factor $Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R} = \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}} = \frac{f_0}{\text{BW}}$!

keyFormulas.label: Series RLC Impedance, Resonant Frequency & Q-Factor
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute resonant frequency, half-power bandwidth, Q-factor, and voltage magnification.

examples.problemLatex: A series RLC circuit with $R = 10\,\Omega,\; L = 0.1\text{ H},\; C = 10\,\mu\text{F}$ is excited at resonance. Find $\omega_0$, quality factor $Q$, and bandwidth in $\text{rad/s}$.

notes.heading: 3. Active, Reactive & Apparent Power Triangle
notes.proseLatex: Using RMS magnitudes $V, I$ and impedance phase $\phi$: Active (real) power $P = VI\cos\phi = I^2 R$ ($\text{W}$), Reactive power $Q = VI\sin\phi = I^2(X_L - X_C)$ ($\text{VAR}$), and Apparent power $S = VI = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2}$ ($\text{VA}$), with power factor $\cos\phi = R/|Z| = P/S$ (pure $L$ or pure $C$ consumes ZERO average real power, $\cos\phi = 0$!). In balanced $3$-phase circuits: Star ($\text{Y}$) has $V_L = \sqrt{3}V_{\text{ph}},\; I_L = I_{\text{ph}}$; Delta ($\Delta$) has $V_L = V_{\text{ph}},\; I_L = \sqrt{3}I_{\text{ph}}$; and BOTH obey $P_{3\phi} = \sqrt{3}V_L I_L\cos\phi$.

keyFormulas.label: AC Power Triangle & Balanced 3-Phase Power
keyFormulas.latex: $P = VI\cos\phi,\quad Q = VI\sin\phi,\quad S = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2},\quad P_{3\phi} = \sqrt{3}\,V_L I_L\cos\phi$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Calculate real/reactive/apparent power, power factor, and 3-phase Y/Delta line relations.

workedExamples.problemLatex: A series RLC circuit with $R = 10\,\Omega,\; L = 0.1\text{ H},\; C = 10\,\mu\text{F}$ is excited at resonance. Find $\omega_0$, quality factor $Q$, and bandwidth in $\text{rad/s}$.

wbjeebTraps: Series vs Parallel resonance flip: SERIES resonance gives MINIMUM $|Z| = R$ and MAXIMUM current; PARALLEL (tank) resonance gives MAXIMUM $|Z|$ (rejector circuit) and MINIMUM line current!
Never add AC series branch voltages algebraically: $V_S = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}$, so at resonance $V_L = V_C = QV_S$ can easily exceed supply voltage $V_S$!
Remember bandwidth units: $\Delta\omega = R/L$ is in $\text{rad/s}$, whereas $\Delta f = \frac{R}{2\pi L}$ is in $\text{Hz}$!
